respect-the-exhale.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: Finished square 1024x1024 song title artwork for track 6 of Grief without Ritual, designed to read clearly as a small album-player cover.
Primary request: Fresh title art for "Respect the Exhale", a restless dry swamp-shuffle blues rock song at 98 BPM. A seasoned, husky, tired female voice gradually eases behind an insistent bass pulse; she loosens her grip while the world keeps moving. Acceptance without triumph. Translate rhythmic pressure and chosen release into a single compelling vintage industrial instruction illustration.
Style/medium: flat printed midcentury workshop manual crossed with a bold music broadside. Aged warm cream paper, slightly uneven black ink, fine engraved crosshatching, worn letterpress grain, restrained rusty brick-red spot ink. Thin distressed black border inset from all four edges. Beautifully composed with tactile detail and useful negative space, no photographic lighting or 3D.
Composition: Top 38-42 percent is enormous tall tightly condensed bold uppercase title, arranged in two lines. Line 1 exact text "RESPECT THE" in black. Line 2 exact text "EXHALE" in rusty brick red. Heavy confident type, exceptional thumbnail legibility, consistent with vintage industrial posters.
Lower image: one coherent, elegantly understandable mechanical diagram. A battered spring-loaded pressure-release valve and its rounded metal chamber mounted to a modest worn workshop base. The outlet is open, a few fine curved lines show air escaping gently into a broad area of clean paper at right. A pressure gauge needle rests low. At left an old belt-driven flywheel is still turning, indicated by a few restrained curved motion marks; the drive belt connects into this same small mechanism. The motor continues, but the pressure is released. The valve lever is eased back, not a dramatic explosion. This is a dry, imperfect, slightly crooked workshop machine, drawn with the soulful wear of an old tube amplifier, small scratches, bolt heads, crosshatching. Mechanical drawing is the main image, not a flowchart, no separate panels. Air and negative space are as important as machinery.
Small figure identifier under title at upper left of illustration: exact "FIG. 6".
Only three fine leader-line labels, readable small condensed uppercase: "PULSE: CONTINUES" at the flywheel; "PRESSURE: RELEASING" at the open valve; "LEAVE THE SPACE" in the open air to the right.
Small understated instruction box in lower left with exact text on three lines: "1. LOOSEN YOUR GRIP." "2. LET IT PASS." "3. LEAVE THE STILLNESS."
Mood: weathered, warm, wry, unhurried release against continuing motion. Intimate blues-rock rather than wellness imagery. Keep the paper spacious, the machine tactile, and the visual hierarchy very strong.
Constraints: all lettering exact and crisp. No artist name, album name, subtitle, extra slogan, invented words, watermarks, collage mockup, LP record border, modern UI, phone, people, smoke cloud, lightning, meditation symbols, decorative musical notes, glossy gradients, heroic uplift. Deliver only the finished square cover, edge to edge.
respect-the-exhale.revisionPrompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Edit target: the supplied Respect the Exhale song cover.
Primary change: Make the lower machine illustration a strict flat industrial engineering diagram, not a rendered or shaded illustration. The current drawing feels much too three-dimensional, pictorial and textural.

Preserve the exact title "RESPECT THE" on the top line in heavy black condensed uppercase, "EXHALE" on the second line in rusty brick red, thin black inset border, warm cream paper, square composition, and exact figure number "FIG. 6". Keep the machinery-continuing / pressure-releasing concept, but completely redraw the machine as a restrained professional technical manual plate.

Diagram specification: Orthographic SIDE ELEVATION only, absolutely no perspective or isometric view. Simple belt-driven flywheel at left, a small pump chamber at center, spring-loaded relief valve and outlet at right, assembled into ONE legible connected mechanical schematic on a thin horizontal baseline. Use clean uniform fine black pen strokes, empty cream interiors, clear circles, centerline crosses, dashed hidden lines, a few small dimension ticks, precise bolts drawn as simple circles. Show the pump chamber in simple cutaway with a few widely spaced diagonal hatch marks ONLY on the actual sliced wall. The flywheel is a thin outlined circle with four simple spokes, NOT a thick black wheel. The belt is two fine parallel straight lines; no shaded tread. The pressure gauge is an outlined circle with five ticks and a single needle resting low. The relief valve is just an outlined valve body, a drawn coil spring, and a plain straight lever. Air leaves the outlet as three sparse curved arrows into generous blank paper. Two small rotation arrows around the flywheel. No heavy solid-black areas except the headline; line weight hierarchy is subtle and technical.

Typography of annotations: compact small uppercase sans-serif, crisp and functional, with fine straight leader lines ending in a dot. Exact labels "PULSE: CONTINUES", "PRESSURE: RELEASING", "LEAVE THE SPACE". Small unshaded rectangular instruction box along lower left, text exactly "1. LOOSEN YOUR GRIP." then "2. LET IT PASS." then "3. LEAVE THE STILLNESS."
Let the technical drawing occupy the lower half with ample negative space around it. Feels like a genuine 1940s pump maintenance manual diagram printed beneath a bold music poster headline. Title can retain moderate letterpress wear, but the diagram must be spare and legible. Light paper age only.

Remove: all volumetric shading, engraved surface rendering, dense crosshatching, woodgrain base, worn rusty metal surface depiction, perspective depth, lighting, shadows, realistic textures on machine, dramatic forms, elaborate supporting machinery, photorealism, 3D.
Do not add any words, album name, artist name, extra panels, or decorative illustrations. Deliver only the finished square cover.
